fullPassage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they include information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.

However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they include information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally __________. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"사람의 삶을 숫자로 바꾸는 것은 도덕적으로 __________ 것이다."

det.tip: insulating = 차단하는, 절연하는. insulate(절연하다)의 현재분사형.

"숫자를 주의해서 정량화하라."
→ __________ with caution.

det.tip: quantify = 수량화하다, 정량화하다. 명령문이므로 동사 원형.

다음 조건에 맞게 영어 문장을 완성하시오.

"숫자는 세상의 더 적절한 그림이 아니다."
→ Numbers are no more __________ 'pictures of the world' than words.

(조건: 1단어)

det.korean: 숫자는 말보다 더 적절한(appropriate) 세상의 그림이 아니다.
det.analysis: 원문 'Numbers are no more appropriate pictures of the world than words'
det.tip: appropriate = 적절한. no more A than B = B만큼 A가 아닌.
